title: SYSK Selects: That Dang-old Goat Fell Over
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the 2011 episode on fainting goats (myotonic goats). Josh introduces the pick, then the hosts cover the goat's association with Satanism (Baphomet, Mendes, Pan, Knights Templar), the fainting goat videos on YouTube, myotonia congenita and the CLCN1 chloride channel gene, the hypnic jerk and myoclonus, the history of the breed from John Tinsley in Marshall County, Tennessee, in the 1880s, its use as meat and novelty animals, the idea of using them as sacrificial protectors against predators, and ethics of unnatural selection (PETA and Humane Society). The episode closes with a listener letter from Ed in Chico, California, a crime scene investigator, about real CSI work versus TV, and the sign-off.

segments.title: Selects intro and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh introduces this week's select, the 2011 episode on fainting goats, and the hosts open with small talk about Chuck feeling sick after Los Angeles.

segments.title: Goats and Satanic symbolism
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Baphomet goat-head image, the Mendes people of Egypt who venerated male goats as fertility symbols as described by Herodotus, the Greek god Pan, and how the goat became associated with Satanism through the Knights Templar.

segments.title: Fainting goat videos and names
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck suggest watching fainting goat videos on YouTube, mention other names such as Tennessee stiff legs and wooden legs, and describe how the goats stiffen and fall over when startled.

segments.title: Myotonia congenita and the chloride gene
segments.summary: The hosts explain myotonia congenita as a congenital nervous system disorder causing muscles to stay stiff, note that it affects people too, and describe the CLCN1 chloride channel gene defect that leaves muscles slow to relax. They also discuss hereditary dominant and recessive patterns.

segments.title: Hypnic jerk and myoclonus
segments.summary: The hosts compare the goats' condition to myoclonus and the hypnic jerk, the sudden jolt people feel when falling asleep, and speculate on why it happens.

segments.title: History of the breed and unnatural selection
segments.summary: John Tinsley is said to have brought the goats from Nova Scotia to Marshall County, Tennessee, in the 1880s, and began breeding them. The hosts discuss breeding for meat and novelty, the lean muscle, the possible use of fainting goats as sacrificial protectors against predators, and the ethics of artificial selection raised by PETA and the Humane Society.

segments.title: Personal goat stories
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh share personal anecdotes about pet goats, and Josh describes a goat at a Santa Barbara winery that Emily held.

segments.title: Listener mail from Ed in Chico about crime scene work
segments.summary: Ed, a crime scene investigator in rural northern California, writes about his multi-role job, the use of point-and-shoot cameras, blood shadows, and how TV crime shows misrepresent DNA and latent print timelines.

segments.title: Outro and how to get in touch
segments.summary: The hosts invite listeners to find the show on Facebook and Twitter, join the QuakeBox team, email about artificial selection, and point to Robert Lamb's article on How Fainting Goats Work.
